correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the Hamming geodesic rectangle identity and characterized a minimal rooted premise B via coordinate-matching row sets M_i: every M_i is nonempty and each row a has a private coordinate with M_i={a}. Singleton patterns are pairwise private, so 2<=r<=d; inclusion-exclusion counts all labeled rows with these singleton types, and private coordinates force distinct rows and prohibit x as a premise, justifying division by r!. For r=d each coordinate has one unique singleton and yields (q-1)^(d(d-1)). A one-pass unit rule deriving x from a minimal stem can have no smaller premise, proving forced canonical basis. The lower bound fixes r~d/2 private columns and varies remaining nonempty matching patterns to get exp(Omega(d^2)), while a pairwise interval-rule system repeatedly reaches hull in O(|V|^3). Independent direct stem/deletion enumeration compared 12 rank cases across (d,q)=(2,2),(3,2),(4,2),(2,3),(3,3),(2,4),(3,4), all matching; d=3,q=3 counts are 36 and 64. Finite checks are not the all-parameter proof.
